evidence: Receiving DO2: 11.41 mg/L at 50.0 h dropping to 1.90 at 50.2 h and 1.60 at 52.0 h — below the 2.0 mg/L operating limit (receiving_observations)
Receiving P assays: 0.026 g/L (24 h), 1.094 g/L (36 h), 3.059 g/L (48 h) — batch otherwise healthy and comparable to source batches (3.02–3.06 g/L at 48 h)
Forward model: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (5.55 mg·h/L) and highest min DO (1.04) and highest product mass (194.5 kg) among all actions
Forward model: increase_air worsens deficit (9.64) vs keep (6.89), indicating DO drawdown is demand-driven rather than transfer-limited
All five ensemble members infeasible for every action — nominal model predicts no action fully restores DO ≥ 2.0
submission.rationale: At ~50.2 h the receiving DO2 collapsed from ~11 to ~1.6–1.9 mg/L, breaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum for ~2 h up to the 52 h decision point. Source-calibrated forward modeling shows the drawdown is oxygen-demand-driven: increase_air alone worsens the deficit, while feed reduction relieves it. Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) achieves the lowest post-decision oxygen deficit (5.55 vs 6.89 for keep), the highest minimum DO (1.04 vs 0.91), and the highest retained product mass (194.5 kg), avoiding a stop (zero counted production). I pair it with continued aeration at 1.15x (the combined lever) since air increase alone is insufficient but supports recovery margin.
submission.uncertainty: The nominal model is source-calibrated and imperfect; hidden receiving parameters (kLa, OUR kinetics) may differ. All model ensemble members remain infeasible (min DO < 2.0) under every action, so full constraint compliance is not guaranteed — strong_feed_reduction merely minimizes violation magnitude and duration. If DO continues falling despite the feed cut, escalation to stop may be warranted by the 56 h sensor window; continued online DO2 monitoring is essential. Assay lag (4 h) means product-state confirmation arrives late.
